prompt: Describe a time you turned an ambiguous request into an actionable goal. What did you personally clarify and how did you know it helped?
provenance: Original synthetic answer authored for mockr; not an actual candidate or human-scored label.

transcript.answer: Last spring our community repair group had a vague request to make signups easier. Volunteers had been manually correcting dates each week, but nobody had measured where the confusion started.
I owned investigation and a proposal within one week. The coordinator owned the final decision. Success meant choosing a change supported by evidence rather than adding every requested feature.

I reviewed twenty synthetic practice signup records, interviewed three volunteers and sketched two options. I chose a clearer date label over a complete form rewrite because the observed confusion clustered around the label.

In the next twenty trial signups, date corrections fell from six to two. The sample was small and could reflect the different volunteers. The coordinator accepted a limited rollout with weekly checks.
I learned that agreement on the symptom was not agreement on the goal. Next time I would set the measurement window before choosing a solution and include users who abandoned the form.
